title: LASA Pair Recognition
description: Identify common confused pairs from the ISMP 2023 list.

questions.prompt: Which medication is a documented Look-Alike / Sound-Alike counterpart to Abelcet?
questions.explanation: Abelcet (amphotericin B lipid complex) is frequently confused with conventional amphotericin B. Mix-ups between formulations can cause severe dosing and toxicity errors.

questions.prompt: Accupril (quinapril) is commonly confused with which medication due to phonetic and orthographic similarity?
questions.explanation: Accupril (an ACE inhibitor for hypertension) and Aciphex (rabeprazole, a PPI for acid reflux) look and sound similar, despite having completely different therapeutic indications.

questions.prompt: Which of the following represents a documented LASA hazard between an analgesic and a glaucoma agent?
questions.explanation: acetaminophen and acetaZOLAMIDE share overlapping prefix letters. Confusion between an over-the-counter analgesic and a prescription carbonic anhydrase inhibitor can lead to treatment failure.

questions.prompt: acetaZOLAMIDE and acetoHEXAMIDE are recognized by ISMP as a Look-Alike, Sound-Alike pair.
questions.explanation: True. acetaZOLAMIDE (carbonic anhydrase inhibitor) and acetoHEXAMIDE (sulfonylurea antidiabetic) are a classic LASA pair that utilize Tall Man lettering to prevent dangerous confusion.

questions.prompt: In the LASA pair Accupril and Aciphex, what is the primary risk factor for medication errors?
choices: Phonetic sound-alike and visual look-alike brand names
questions.correctAnswer: Phonetic sound-alike and visual look-alike brand names
questions.explanation: Accupril and Aciphex belong to completely different drug classes (ACE inhibitor vs PPI), but verbal orders and similar written spelling frequently lead to selection errors.

title: Tall Man Lettering Basics
description: Practice distinguishing medication pairs using uppercase Tall Man formatting.

questions.prompt: Which drug uses Tall Man lettering to distinguish it from the antidiabetic acetoHEXAMIDE?
questions.explanation: acetaZOLAMIDE capitalizes ZOLAMIDE to emphasize the difference from acetoHEXAMIDE, which capitalizes HEXAMIDE.

questions.prompt: Why is Tall Man lettering used on medication packaging and electronic health records?
choices: To draw visual attention to differing letters in look-alike names
To indicate the strength and dosage of the pill
To show that the drug is an over-the-counter medication
To represent the manufacturer's trademark styling
questions.correctAnswer: To draw visual attention to differing letters in look-alike names
questions.explanation: Tall Man lettering is a medication safety technique recommended by ISMP and the FDA that capitalizes unique letter sequences to disrupt visual confusion.

questions.prompt: Tall Man lettering was created purely for aesthetic design rather than medication error prevention.
questions.explanation: False. Tall Man lettering is an evidence-based clinical safety standard specifically designed to reduce adverse drug events caused by look-alike medication names.
